title: I Connected 3 MCP Servers to One Agent. It Got Scary Fast.
excerpt: I looked at my terminal last week and realized my AI agent had the same access to deploy production...
content_html:
I looked at my terminal last week and realized my AI agent had the same access to deploy production as it did to search a README. No policy. No approvals. No audit trail. Three MCP servers wired directly in, side by side, identical trust.

The first two were fine — docs search, code search. Read-only. The third could promote builds to production. And that's when it clicked: MCP standardized how agents talk to tools, but did absolutely nothing for what happens after you connect more than a couple of them.

The official MCP servers repo has 88,900 stars and 11,300 forks. Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, Cursor — they all speak MCP. There's a registry for browsing servers. The ecosystem is taking off, and I couldn't find a single governance tool for any of it.

What I tried first

Three paths. None of them worked.

API gateways route HTTP. They don't understand MCP tool schemas. You can't write a rule that says "this agent can use deployment:promote but not deployment:rollback" — the gateway doesn't know what those are.

Custom middleware works until the person who built it leaves and nobody understands how the approval chain works. No UI. Every new server requires code changes.

Nothing — just wire servers directly and trust the agent code. This was my setup. It felt fine at two servers. At three, I couldn't answer "what can this agent actually do?"

So I started building.

The roadmap died on day three

I had a plan. v0.1.0: API — servers, capabilities, policies. v0.2.0: Admin UI and approvals. v0.3.0: audit, alerts, trust posture.

Then I realized a control plane without a UI isn't a control plane at all. Nobody curls an endpoint to see which servers are registered or which approvals are pending. The UI was supposed to be a v0.2 feature. I pulled it into v0.1.0.

Same thing happened with approvals. Then audit. Then alerts. Each layer depended on the one before it. Cutting any of them meant cutting the core promise: "see, control, and audit what your agents do." By the time I stopped, v0.1.0 had absorbed most of v0.2 and v0.3. Three planned layers became eight.

I don't know if that was smart or stubborn. It tripled the timeline. But shipping disconnected pieces that wouldn't make sense until months later felt worse.

Where the time actually went

The backend took days. FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, OPA — standard stack.

What ate weeks:

The PRD and Customer User Journeys. Before writing a single component, I mapped every flow: register a server, review an approval, audit an incident. What happens when it fails? Empty states, error states, permission-denied states. Every CUJ forced answers the API never asked for. I kept wondering if I was over-planning.

The UI. Originally v0.2. Bringing it into v0.1 meant navigation, error boundaries, trust posture color coding, role-based filtering, the approval panel — every screen end-to-end. Then testing it. Sixty-eight Playwright E2E scenarios. Backend tests ran in seconds. UI tests took forever.

CI. Poetry v2 dropped --no-update. npm 11 rejected TypeScript peer deps. Neither had anything to do with my code. A day fixing infrastructure that "already worked."

Mypy. 170 type errors across 41 files. Every one was a design decision I'd been sloppy about, disguised as a type violation. Strict mode didn't let me hide.

PyPI. Three attempts. mcp-fabric was taken. mcpfabric blocked. fabric-mcp blocked. Fourth try: mcp-fabric-toolmesh.

The number I keep coming back to: 170 type errors across 41 files. That's not bugs. That's unclear thinking, surfaced by a tool that refused to let it slide.

What came out

You register MCP servers and Fabric auto-discovers their tools. Raw tool names normalize into domain-level capabilities — /promoteDeploy and /promote both map to deployment:promote. Every request hits OPA policies. Sensitive capabilities can require human approval. Everything is logged. Alerts fire when servers degrade. Identity tokens per agent class. Capability packs for permission bundling.

474 tests. Six parallel CI jobs. Published to PyPI. Open source.

I've been running it against my own three servers. Before Fabric, every token had access to everything. Now the developer agent searches docs and code. The release engineer requests deployment — but it pauses for approval. The difference between "trust the code" and "verify every request" took 30 minutes of configuration.

What I'd do differently

PRD and CUJs on day one, not after the API. I built the backend first, then designed the UI around it. Backwards. The CUJ mapping caught gaps the API missed.

The UI is not a v0.2 feature. If your tool needs human interaction, the UI is MVP. Designing the API for curl and the UI for humans meant refactoring when they didn't match.

Scope consolidation is not scope creep. Packing 0.2 and 0.3 into 0.1 looked like bad planning. In hindsight, each layer depended on the previous. The real mistake was the original roadmap pretending they were independent.

I'm still figuring out if tool governance should be a layer on top of MCP, or something the spec itself eventually absorbs. I built what I needed for my setup — I don't know if it generalizes.

If you're running MCP servers: how are you handling this? Wiring directly and hoping? Writing middleware? Waiting for the ecosystem? I suspect most people's answer is "we're not handling it yet," and that feels like a conversation worth having.

July 25, 2026: v0.3.0 — Security Hardening & Compliance
Full Changelog (https://github.com/deghosal-2026/mcp-fabric/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

Schema-Digest Mappings detect tool schema drift by storing a SHA-256 hash of each capability mapping at creation time. When a server re-inspect reveals a changed schema, affected mappings are automatically marked stale and excluded from routing until an admin reviews and approves — closing the gap between registered schemas and runtime reality.
Also in this release:

  • OPA deny rules — deny_stale_mapping blocks stale mappings, untrusted_write blocks writes on unreviewed servers
  • Pack breadth warnings — visual catch-rate indicators in the pack editor and Trust Posture dashboard (4 severity tiers)
  • Audit enrichment — pack resource counts and implied catch-rate in every audit event, queryable via filter
  • Reviews UI — approve/reject workflow for stale mappings with audit trail
  • 10 new OPA rules (31 total), 326 Python tests, 75 Playwright E2E tests pip install --upgrade mcp-fabric-toolmesh

blocks.html_en: I've been running it against my own three servers. Before Fabric, every token had access to everything. Now the developer agent searches docs and code. The release engineer requests deployment — but it pauses for approval. The difference between "trust the code" and "verify every request" took 30 minutes of configuration.

blocks.html_en: Scope consolidation is not scope creep. Packing 0.2 and 0.3 into 0.1 looked like bad planning. In hindsight, each layer depended on the previous. The real mistake was the original roadmap pretending they were independent.

blocks.html_en: I'm still figuring out if tool governance should be a layer on top of MCP, or something the spec itself eventually absorbs. I built what I needed for my setup — I don't know if it generalizes.

Schema-Digest Mappings detect tool schema drift by storing a SHA-256 hash of each capability mapping at creation time. When a server re-inspect reveals a changed schema, affected mappings are automatically marked stale and excluded from routing until an admin reviews and approves — closing the gap between registered schemas and runtime reality.
Also in this release:

content_html_zh:
上周我查看了我的终端，意识到我的人工智能代理具有与搜索自述文件相同的访问权限来部署生产。 没有政策。 没有批准。 没有审计线索。 三个 MCP 服务器直接并排连接，具有相同的信任。

前两个很好——文档搜索、代码搜索。 只读。 第三个可以促进构建到生产。 就在那时，它突然出现了：MCP 标准化了代理与工具的对话方式，但对于连接多个工具后发生的情况完全没有任何作用。

官方 MCP 服务器存储库拥有 88,900 个 star 和 11,300 个 fork。 Claude、ChatGPT、VS Code、Cursor——它们都讲 MCP。 有一个用于浏览服务器的注册表。 生态系统正在起飞，但我找不到任何一个单一的治理工具。

我首先尝试的

三个路径。 他们都没有工作。

API 网关路由 HTTP。 他们不理解 MCP 工具架构。 您不能编写一条规则来说明“此代理可以使用部署：升级，但不能使用部署：回滚” - 网关不知道这些是什么。

自定义中间件可以一直工作，直到构建它的人离开并且没有人了解审批链是如何工作的。 没有用户界面 每个新服务器都需要更改代码。

没什么——只是直接连接服务器并信任代理代码。 这是我的设置。 在两台服务器上感觉很好。 三岁时，我无法回答“这个代理实际上能做什么？”

所以我开始建造。

路线图在第三天就失效了

我有一个计划。 v0.1.0：API — 服务器、功能、策略。 v0.2.0：管理 UI 和批准。 v0.3.0：审核、警报、信任状态。

然后我意识到没有 UI 的控制平面根本就不是控制平面。 没有人通过卷曲端点来查看哪些服务器已注册或哪些审批正在等待。 UI 应该是 v0.2 的功能。 我把它拉到了 v0.1.0 中。

批准也发生了同样的事情。 然后审核。 然后警报。 每一层都依赖于它之前的一层。 削减其中任何一项都意味着削减核心承诺：“查看、控制和审计您的代理的行为。” 当我停止时，v0.1.0 已经吸收了 v0.2 和 v0.3 的大部分内容。 计划的三层变成了八层。

我不知道这是聪明还是固执。 它使时间线增加了两倍。 但运送不连贯的部件直到几个月后才有意义，感觉更糟。

时间到底去哪儿了

后端花了几天时间。 FastAPI、PostgreSQL、Redis、OPA — 标准堆栈。

几周吃了什么：

PRD 和客户用户旅程。 在编写单个组件之前，我映射了每个流程：注册服务器、审查批准、审核事件。 失败时会发生什么？ 空状态、错误状态、权限被拒绝状态。 每个 CUJ 都强制回答 API 从未要求过的问题。 我一直在想我是否计划过度了。

用户界面。 最初是 v0.2。 将其引入 v0.1 意味着导航、错误边界、信任状态颜色编码、基于角色的过滤、审批面板 - 每个屏幕端到端。 然后测试一下。 68 个剧作家 E2E 场景。 后端测试在几秒钟内运行。 UI 测试花了很长时间。

那里。 Poetry v2 已删除——无更新。 npm 11 拒绝了 TypeScript 对等部门。 两者都与我的代码无关。 修复“已经起作用”的基础设施的一天。

我的。 41 个文件中有 170 个类型错误。 每一个都是我草率做出的设计决定，伪装成类型违规。 严格模式没有让我隐藏。

PyPI。 三次尝试。 mcp-fabric 已被占用。 mcpfabric 被阻止。 Fabric-MCP 被阻止。 第四次尝试：mcp-fabric-toolmesh。

我不断回想起的数字是：41 个文件中有 170 个类型错误。 那不是错误。 这是一种不明确的想法，是由一个拒绝让它滑动的工具浮现出来的。

出来了什么

您注册 MCP 服务器，Fabric 会自动发现它们的工具。 原始工具名称标准化为域级功能 - /promoteDeploy 和 /promote 都映射到部署：promote。 每个请求都符合 OPA 政策。 敏感功能可能需要人类批准。 一切都被记录下来。 当服务器性能下降时会发出警报。 每个代理类别的身份令牌。 用于权限捆绑的功能包。

474 次测试。 六个并行 CI 作业。 发布到 PyPI。 开源。

我一直在我自己的三台服务器上运行它。 在 Fabric 之前，每个代币都可以访问所有内容。 现在，开发人员代理搜索文档和代码。 发布工程师请求部署 - 但它会暂停以等待批准。 “信任代码”和“验证每个请求”之间的区别需要 30 分钟的配置。

我会采取什么不同的做法

PRD 和 CUJ 在第一天，而不是在 API 之后。 我首先构建了后端，然后围绕它设计了 UI。 向后。 CUJ 映射抓住了 API 错过的空白。

UI 不是 v0.2 功能。 如果您的工具需要人机交互，那么 UI 就是 MVP。 为curl 设计API 并为人类设计UI 意味着在它们不匹配时进行重构。

范围整合不是范围蔓延。 将 0.2 和 0.3 打包到 0.1 中看起来是一个糟糕的计划。 事后看来，每一层都依赖于前一层。 真正的错误是最初的路线图假装他们是独立的。

我仍在弄清楚工具治理是否应该是 MCP 之上的一层，或者规范本身最终吸收的东西。 我构建了我的设置所需的东西 - 我不知道它是否具有普遍性。

如果您正在运行 MCP 服务器：您如何处理这个问题？ 直接接线并希望吗？ 写中间件？ 等待生态系统？ 我怀疑大多数人的答案是“我们还没有处理它”，这感觉像是一场值得进行的对话。

2026 年 7 月 25 日：v0.3.0 — 安全强化和合规性完整变更日志 (https://github.com/deghosal-2026/mcp-fabric/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

模式摘要映射通过在创建时存储每个功能映射的 SHA-256 哈希来检测工具模式漂移。 当服务器重新检查发现更改的架构时，受影响的映射会自动标记为过时，并从路由中排除，直到管理员审核并批准 - 缩小注册架构和运行时现实之间的差距。 在此版本中还有：

  • OPA拒绝规则——deny_stale_mapping阻止过时的映射，untrusted_write阻止在未经审查的服务器上写入
  • 包广度警告 - 包编辑器和信任状态仪表板中的可视捕获率指示器（4 个严重级别）
  • 审计丰富——每个审计事件中的资源计数和隐含捕获率，可通过过滤器查询
  • 审查 UI — 通过审核跟踪批准/拒绝陈旧映射的工作流程
  • 10 个新的 OPA 规则（总共 31 个）、326 个 Python 测试、75 个 Playwright E2E 测试 pip install --upgrade mcp-fabric-toolmesh
